n: Saul's jealousy comes into the open: he orders Jonathan and all his servants to kill David.
Jonathan, who loves David deeply, warns him of the danger and tells him to hide until morning. Loyalty to righteousness outweighs loyalty to his father's sin.
Jonathan plans to talk with his father in the field near David's hiding place and report back what he learns.
Jonathan speaks up for David, urging his father not to sin against an innocent man whose deeds had only helped him. A courageous act of a peacemaker.
Jonathan reminds Saul that David risked his life against Goliath and that the Lord saved Israel through him. Why shed innocent blood without cause?

f.w: put his life in his hand

n: Saul listens and swears by the Lord that David will not be killed. For a moment Saul's better side wins out.
Jonathan tells David everything and brings him back to court, where he serves Saul as before.
War breaks out again, and David wins a great victory over the Philistines — which reignites Saul's jealousy.
The troubling spirit again comes upon Saul as he sits holding a spear, while David plays music.

f.w: the evil spirit from the LORD
f.g: JST: “the evil spirit which was not of God.”

n: Saul tries again to pin David to the wall with the spear, but David slips away and the spear sticks in the wall. David flees that night.

f.w: smite David even to the wall

n: Saul sends men to watch David's house and kill him in the morning. Michal warns David that he must escape tonight or die tomorrow.

f.g: The heading of Psalm 59 connects that psalm to this event.

n: Michal lowers David out through a window, and he escapes — like Rahab helping the spies escape Jericho.

f.w: let David down through a window

n: Michal puts a household idol in the bed, with goat hair at the head and a covering over it, to look like David sleeping. That David's home had such an idol is a surprising detail.

f.g: Hebrew teraphim — household idols or figurines.

n: When Saul's men come, Michal tells them David is sick, buying him time.
Saul orders them to bring David in his bed so he can kill him — showing how ruthless he has become.
The men find only the idol with goat hair in the bed. The trick is discovered.
Saul accuses Michal of betrayal. She protects herself with a lie, claiming David threatened to kill her if she didn't help.
David flees to Samuel at Ramah and tells him everything. They go together to Naioth, perhaps a settlement where prophets lived.

f.g: Probably “dwellings” — a group of houses for the prophets near Ramah.

n: Someone reports to Saul that David is at Naioth in Ramah.
Saul sends men to arrest David, but when they see the prophets prophesying with Samuel leading them, the Spirit of God comes on them and they prophesy too. God protects David by His Spirit.
Saul sends a second and third group, and each is overcome by the Spirit and prophesies. No human force can stand against the Lord's power.
Finally Saul goes himself. At the large well in Sechu he asks where Samuel and David are and is told Naioth.

f.g: A place near Ramah whose location is unknown.

n: On the way, the Spirit of God comes even on Saul, and he prophesies all the way to Naioth. The same Spirit that once empowered him now stops him in his tracks.
Saul strips off his royal robes and lies on the ground before Samuel all day and night. This humiliating scene revives the old saying, “Is Saul also among the prophets?”

f.g: Probably stripped of his outer royal garments, not fully unclothed.

f.w: Is Saul also among the prophets?
